Report_ID: Bundle 1 (Early Hours) all-or-none compliance, Oct-Dec 2009 (end of intervention period)
Title: Did a quality improvement collaborative make stroke care better? A cluster randomized trial
Author: Power et al.
Comment: The odds ratio 1.56 is a difference-in-difference (interaction) estimate from a random-effects logistic regression accounting for hospital clustering, not a simple post-period intervention-vs-control contrast. Event counts shown are the Oct-Dec 2009 post-intervention period only (baseline Oct-Dec 2008 was 114/583 intervention, 122/502 control, favouring control). Trial-reported ICC for this outcome = 0.066; average cluster size approx 610/9 and 566/9 in the post period.
Design Type: cluster randomized controlled trial with interrupted time series / difference-in-difference analysis
domain: implementation science / acute stroke quality improvement
Participant type: patients admitted with acute stroke in NHS hospitals
Recruitment source: NHS hospital Trusts in the Northwest of England with a stroke unit of at least ten inpatient beds
Outcome measurement: Proportion of audited stroke patients receiving all four early-hours bundle elements
Outcome variable: Bundle 1 (Early Hours) all-or-none compliance, Oct-Dec 2009 (end of intervention period)
outcome_family: Adherence to evidence-based recommended processes of acute stroke care

Report_ID: Proportion of stroke cases treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IVT rate), postintervention period — primary outcome
Title: Cluster-Randomized Trial of Thrombolysis Implementation Support in Metropolitan and Regional Australian Stroke Centers: Lessons for Individual and Systems Behavior Change
Author: Levi CR, Attia JA, D'Este C, et al.
Comment: Cluster-randomized trial; no ICC reported (sample size used a coefficient of variation of 0.4), so SE inflation for the design effect would require an assumed ICC (e.g. 0.05) downstream. M_diff=1.1 is the prespecified adjusted ABSOLUTE rate difference in percentage points (adjusted for baseline rate and stratum); its reported CI is printed as "1.5% to 3.7%" with minus signs apparently lost in typesetting (Discussion gives "1.1% (95% CI 2.8% to 5.1%)" for the within-stratum very-low value), so no SE_diff was derived. No cluster-adjusted RR/OR for this comparison is reported.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Implementation package (intervention) hospitals (n=10 clusters)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: patients hospitalised with acute stroke (hospitals as unit of randomization)
Recruitment source: 20 Australian hospitals (NSW, Victoria, Queensland) in early stages of thrombolysis implementation
Outcome measurement: Patient-level count of thrombolysed stroke cases out of all stroke separations per arm
Outcome variable: Proportion of stroke cases treated with intravenous thrombolysis (IVT rate), postintervention period — primary outcome
outcome_family: Adherence to evidence-based recommended processes of acute stroke care

Report_ID: Swallowing screening within 24 h of admission to ASU (proportion of patients receiving recommended process of care)
Title: Implementation of evidence-based treatment protocols to manage fever, hyperglycaemia, and swallowing dysfunction in acute stroke (QASC): a cluster randomised controlled trial
Author: Middleton S, McElduff P, Ward J, Grimshaw JM, Dale S, D'Este C, Drury P, Griffiths R, Cheung NW, Quinn C, Evans M, Cadilhac D, Levi C
Comment: The paper reports only an adjusted absolute difference (29.2%, 95% CI 22.0-36.4; stored in M_diff as percentage points) for this dichotomous outcome — no cluster-adjusted RR or OR with CI is reported, so the pooled RR must be computed from the raw patient-level counts with the SE inflated by the design effect using the trial-reported ICC of 0.156 and mean post-intervention cluster size of 59. p value is reported as <0.0001 and adjusted for clustering (interaction term between group and period).
Design Type: cluster randomised controlled trial (19 clusters; pre- and post-intervention patient cohorts; ICC for this outcome 0.156; mean post-intervention cluster size 59)
Participant type: adult patients (>=18 years) admitted with ischaemic stroke or intracerebral haemorrhage within 48 h of symptom onset to an acute stroke unit
Recruitment source: 19 acute stroke units (Australian National Stroke Unit Program Category A or B) in New South Wales, Australia
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients with a documented swallowing screen within 24 h of ASU admission
Outcome variable: Swallowing screening within 24 h of admission to ASU (proportion of patients receiving recommended process of care)
outcome_family: Adherence to evidence-based recommended processes of acute stroke care

Report_ID: Thrombolysis (rtPA) delivery in patients with ischemic stroke admitted within 4 hours
Title: Promoting Thrombolysis in Acute Ischemic Stroke (PRACTISE trial)
Author: Dirks M, et al.
Comment: Cluster-randomized trial: effect reported as an odds ratio (Table 3 footnote: "Values are numbers and effects in ORs"), adjusted for clustering plus hospital size, academic vs nonacademic, prior thrombolysis rate, age, sex, stroke severity and comorbidity. Paper reports no risk ratio for this outcome, so the ratio fields were left empty rather than inferring an RR. Unadjusted OR 1.24 (1.02-1.51) and cluster-adjusted-only OR 1.44 (0.93-2.22) also reported. Trial-reported ICC for the primary outcome = 0.0154 (design effect 7.35) if SE inflation is needed. This outcome overlaps with the total-population thrombolysis outcome (same patients, nested) - do not double-count.; group_1/group_2 fields swapped: the extractor itself stated group_1_label ('Intervention hospitals (multidimensional Breakthrough Series implementation strategy; 6 clusters)') is the intervention arm (group_1_is_control=False)
Participant type: patients admitted with acute stroke within 24 hours of symptom onset (12 hospitals)
Recruitment source: 12 urban/community, academic/nonacademic hospitals in the Netherlands
Outcome measurement: Number (%) of patients treated with rtPA out of patients with ischemic stroke admitted within 4 hours, per arm
Outcome variable: Thrombolysis (rtPA) delivery in patients with ischemic stroke admitted within 4 hours
outcome_family: Adherence to evidence-based recommended processes of acute stroke care
unit_of_analysis: per eligible patient (ischemic stroke admitted within 4 h)
